extracted.intended_audience: general readers, film fans, critics, and researchers looking for encyclopedic information about the film
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic Wikipedia article summarizing a single film's production, plot, release, reception, and legacy. Contains factual details, critical responses, box-office data, and production notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of grosses and performance versus budget and expectations (e.g., "grossed $64.7 million in the United States and Canada, and $25.3 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $90 million" against a production budget of $30–35 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes opening-day and opening-weekend figures, projections, comparisons with competing releases (released alongside Jesus Revolution and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania), daily/weekly hold/drop percentages ("finished in third place in its sophomore weekend with $11 million (dropping 54%)"), and interpretation of whether holds are "very good" for the genre. Use gross-to-budget ratio, opening weekend receipts, and percentage drops to evaluate commercial success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical aggregator scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of aggregator metrics (e.g., "On Rotten Tomatoes, 66% of 328 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.1/10"; "Metacritic ... assigned the film a score of 54 out of 100"; audience measures: CinemaScore grade and PostTrak positive/recommendation percentages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Rotten Tomatoes % and average rating, Metacritic weighted score and qualitative band ("mixed or average"), and audience polling (CinemaScore letter grade, PostTrak positive and 'definitely recommend' percentages) as standardized indicators of critical and audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot and premise effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical judgments about the film's plot and premise (examples: "half-baked plot", "one-joke premise is stretched thin", "plot twists seem irrelevant").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate originality, coherence, and whether the premise sustains runtime; be alert to criticisms that a high-concept hook can be exhausted if not developed ("the film's one-joke premise is stretched thin").

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters and acting
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical commentary on characters and performances (phrases from reviews: "uneven acting", "criticized the human characters and their interactions", "criticized the number of characters, subplots and pacing").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess number and development of characters, ensemble balance, acting quality, and whether character interactions serve the story. Note critiques that too many characters/subplots can dilute focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and genre balance (horror-comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how effectively the film balances horror and comedy (described as "black comedy/horror film", "blood-splattered major studio horror-comedy", and comments about "violent comedy/thriller").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether tone is consistent and whether horror and comedy elements complement each other; critics noted success in producing "raucous, transgressive moments" and capturing "comic potential of the gross-out," but also that tonal choices may make the film feel uneven or one-note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy effectiveness and gross-out humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews emphasize the film's comedic approach and gross-out elements (examples: "scene-snorting frenzy will give B-movie enthusiasts a contact high", "successfully captures the 'comic potential of the gross-out'").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether comedic beats land, whether gross-out humor is deliberately used and effective for the intended audience, and whether the film functions as escapist B-movie entertainment versus more substantive comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and script economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical remarks about pacing, number of subplots, and script tightness (e.g., criticisms that the film "criticized the number of characters, subplots and pacing", "silly but not stupid", "script becomes sentimentally dutiful at the end").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether runtime is used efficiently, whether subplots distract from central premise, and whether tonal shifts toward sentimentality undermine earlier momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction and production leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and evaluative context about the director and producers (Elizabeth Banks directing; produced by Phil Lord, Christopher Miller, Elizabeth Banks, Max Handelman, Brian Duffield, Aditya Sood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess directorial choices, risk-taking in tone/genre (Banks said the movie could be seen as the bear's 'revenge story'), and producer influence on project development; observers noted the director's role in realizing gory R-rated comedy from an unusual premise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenplay and writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on the screenplay and its handling of material (written by Jimmy Warden; reviewers noted "half-baked plot", irrelevant twists, sentimental ending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate script structure, character economy, relevance of plot twists, and whether the screenplay successfully adapts its high-concept inspiration into a sustained narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual effects and creature performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Details on how the bear was realized (large portion of budget went to Wētā FX to create the bear with CGI; Allan Henry credited as 'Bear Performer' used custom-made limb extensions and provided reference for animators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess quality and believability of creature effects, the integration of practical performance references with CGI, and budget allocation impact (significant VFX spend can be a major production factor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Music and soundtrack
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about film score and soundtrack decisions (Natalie Holt was reported to compose, later replaced by Mark Mothersbaugh; trailer used 'White Lines (Don't Don't Do It)')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider score's contribution to tone and audience experience; note composer changes and use of licensed songs in trailers as part of marketing and tone-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting and performer recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensemble cast listing and performance notes; film dedicated to Ray Liotta after his death; reviewers singled out the bear's 'performance' as praise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate casting fit, ensemble chemistry, and notable performances; dedication and posthumous recognition can affect cultural reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity to real events and creative liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit discussion that the film is 'loosely inspired' by real events and 'differs from real-life events in a number of ways' (the real bear is 'not known to have killed anyone'); director framed it as a revenge story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging based on 'based on a true story' claims, consider accuracy versus creative license, whether deviations are justified artistically, and transparency about fictionalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing, social media virality, and promotional effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes that the story went viral on social media prior to release; trailer reaction and marketing (trailer described as 'insanely fun'); film won several Golden Trailer Awards (Best Comedy, Best Viral Campaign, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure marketing success by social-media engagement, trailer impact, awards for campaign work, and whether promotional tone aligns with the film's content and target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release and distribution strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Release pattern information (theatrical release on February 24, 2023; released on premium video on demand services two weeks after theatrical release; Blu-ray and DVD release on April 18, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timing between theatrical and home release, platform strategy (PVOD window), and how release timing interacts with box-office performance and marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, nominations, and industry recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing of nominations and wins (nominated for MTV Movie & TV Awards Best Villain; won four Golden Trailer Awards categories; nominated for Outstanding Achievement for Character Animation at the Annie Awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nominations/wins as signals of industry recognition in specific areas (marketing, character animation, performance), noting which aspects were honored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural impact and legacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the film's cultural footprint (inspired mockbusters such as Meth Gator and Crackcoon; a documentary 'Cocaine Bear: The True Story' released the same year; the original taxidermied bear on display and the film's role in viral popular culture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess influence by derivative works, spinoffs, mockbusters, documentaries, merchandising/museum displays, and broader social-media and pop-culture references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production logistics and location choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Details about principal photography (took place in County Wicklow, Ireland, from Aug 20 to Oct 17, 2021) and production decisions (Ireland doubling for Georgia/USA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate location choices for cost, practicality, and whether they convincingly represent intended settings; note production schedule and impact on budget.
